changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: When a buyer's finance team starts asking for payback, do not send the general study. Offer instead: Let's build your number together: what your current billing system costs you today and how fast switching pays back. Book that session the week the champion asks for something for finance, and use the result to get in front of the CFO.
changes.why: We sent the generic ROI deck and the champion said plainly "I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours", but the session to build that number never happened before the freeze.

changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For product and engineering leaders running a homegrown billing system, swap the revenue line for: Stop billing being a tax on the roadmap. Change a price, add a trial or set proration in a few clicks, not a quarter of engineering work.
changes.why: The VP of Product rejected the revenue framing outright ("we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap."), and the demo landed because it gave back "a quarter of roadmap in five minutes."

changes.change: For CFO and finance audiences when the alternative is doing nothing: add a cost-of-status-quo proof point that turns the roadmap tax into money. Count engineering time lost per pricing change, the risk of a homegrown system whose builder has left, and revenue lost from subscriptions that lapse when a card fails and nobody chases it. Connect that last item to M10's smart retries. The goal is for the project to read as on fire, not a nice to have.
changes.why: Finance saw the project as a "nice to have" under a rule of "if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded." The rep says the missing piece was "Their own. What the homegrown system costs them", including lapsed subscriptions that "We never added it up."

changes.change: For buyers moving existing subscriptions off a homegrown system: answer migration questions with a reference customer who has done it, not only a doc. Lead with moving existing subscriptions without asking customers for their card details again, and with the option to migrate in stages.
changes.why: The champion asked about migrating without re-collecting card details and doing it in stages. We had a doc, but "He wanted to talk to someone who'd done it."
